# Diagnostics reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run guide` (scripts/user-guide.ts). Don't edit by hand. -->

Every diagnostic CatSpec reports has a stable code. The severity is the default; a spec's
status, `enforcement` settings and waivers can change it (see [the spec format](./spec-format.md)).

## CS0101

**invalid spec** · error

The spec can't be read as a valid spec: the file has no `---` frontmatter or it isn't closed, the YAML is invalid, a required field is missing, or a value has the wrong type or isn't one of the allowed values. The message names the field and the allowed values. Fix the frontmatter at the reported line.

## CS0102

**unknown key** · warning

A top-level frontmatter key that CatSpec doesn't know. It is ignored, so teams can keep their own metadata in the spec. Check the spelling if it was meant to be a CatSpec key.

## CS0103

**duplicate id** · error

Spec ids must be unique across the repository, and binding and rule ids unique within their spec. Rename one of them; the message names every place that uses the id.

## CS0104

**unknown dependency** · error

`depends_on` names a spec id that doesn't exist. Fix the id (the message suggests close matches) or add the missing spec.

## CS0105

**dependency cycle** · error

The `depends_on` relations form a cycle, so no spec in it can ever be started. The message shows the full cycle (`a → b → c → a`); remove one of its dependencies.

## CS0106

**spec outside a feature folder** · warning

With `layout: feature-folders`, every `*.spec.md` lives directly in `docs/spec/<feature>/`, and the architecture spec at the path in `specs.architecture`. Move the file as suggested, or set `layout: free` in `catspec.yaml` if the repository uses another layout.

## CS0107

**architecture spec missing or ambiguous** · error

Exactly one file must match `specs.architecture` (default `docs/architecture/adr/*-adr.md`). Create it with `catspec init`, remove the extra matches, or change `specs.architecture` in `catspec.yaml`. In `check --staged`, an ADR log that exists on disk but isn't staged yet is a warning that names the file to stage, so the first commit after `catspec init` isn't blocked.

## CS0108

**lock file without spec** · warning

A generated `<spec-id>.lock.json` has no spec with that id in its folder, usually because the spec was deleted, renamed or moved without its lock file. Delete the lock file, or move it next to its spec (a spec's lock file is named after its id).

## CS0110

**unknown reference** · error

The spec body references `[rule:<id>]` or `[binding:<id>]`, but the frontmatter has no rule or binding with that id. Fix the reference or add the rule or binding.

## CS0111

**unenforced prose invariant** · warning

A bullet under a `Contracts` or `Invariants` heading has no `[rule:<id>]` or `[binding:<id>]` reference, so nothing checks it. Add a rule (a `manual` rule if it can't be checked from code) and reference it. Controlled by `enforcement.unenforced_prose`.

## CS0112

**unknown ADR id** · error

A rule's `adr` field names a decision that isn't in the architecture spec's ADR log (a `## ADR-NNN: <title>` heading). Fix the id or add the decision to the log.

## CS0130

**invalid query** · error

A `query` rule's Tree-sitter query doesn't compile for its language (for example unbalanced parentheses or an unknown node type), or no language adapter is installed for its `lang`. Queries are compiled when the specs load, before any code is read. Fix the query at the reported line.

## CS0201

**binding not found** · error

No declaration in the code matches the binding's `symbol` (and `kind`). CatSpec looks in the files of the `file` hint first, then in every source file, so a moved file is still found. The message suggests close names of the same kind, in the hinted files first. Fix the symbol, restore the code, or run `catspec sync` after a rename.

## CS0202

**binding ambiguous** · error

More than one declaration matches the binding's `symbol` and they aren't C# `partial` parts of one type. The message lists every location. Qualify the symbol (`Namespace.Type` or `path/to/module#Name`) or add a `file` hint.

## CS0203

**member missing** · error

The bound declaration has no member with the name a `members` entry requires. The message suggests the closest existing members with their location. Add the member, rename it back, mark the entry `optional: true`, or update the spec.

## CS0204

**base type missing** · error

The bound declaration doesn't directly extend or implement a type listed in `implements` or `extends`. Types match by qualified-name suffix and generic arguments. Add the base type or update the spec.

## CS0205

**signature mismatch** · error

A member exists but its kind, parameter types, return type or modifiers differ from the spec. The message shows the expected and the found signature. `*` in `params` matches any type.

## CS0206

**attribute missing** · error

The declaration or member lacks a C# attribute or TypeScript decorator that the spec requires in `attributes`. Names match without a trailing `Attribute`; arguments are compared only when the spec gives them.

## CS0207

**constructor dependency missing** · error

No constructor of the bound class takes every type in `constructor.requires` (dependency injection). The message names the missing types for the closest constructor.

## CS0208

**visibility or export mismatch** · error

`exported` requires the declaration to be exported (TypeScript) or `public` (C#), or not, or a member lacks a required visibility modifier (`public`, `private`, `protected`, `internal`).

## CS0210

**renamed** · error

A declaration a binding pointed to was renamed or moved, and CatSpec found where it went (a rename map, the same name in another file, a namespace or path prefix change, a git file rename, the same shape, or a similarity score at or above `heal.threshold`). The diagnostic carries the location-only patch (`symbol` and `file` only, never the contract). Run `catspec sync --apply`; with `heal.mode: auto` the pre-commit hook applies it and stages the spec. As info, it also reports backticked mentions of the old name in the spec body, rewritten only with `catspec sync --apply --update-mentions`.

## CS0215

**large refactor** · error

Many bindings broke at once: more than `refactor.detect_threshold` in one commit, or any while a refactor (`catspec refactor`) is in progress. The hook reports this one summary instead of a binding, drift or ratchet error per binding. Run `catspec sync` to see the mapping and `catspec sync --apply` to update every spec in one batch. During a refactor started with `--allow-wip` it is a warning on the refactor's branch, so intermediate commits go through.

## CS0216

**ambiguous rename** · error

`catspec sync` can't tell which declaration a binding's old declaration became: several candidates are equally close, or a closer match took the only one. CatSpec never guesses: no spec is changed. The message lists the candidates. Name the rename in a rename map (`{ "symbols": { "Old.Name": "New.Name" } }`) and run `catspec sync --apply --map <file>`, or fix the binding by hand.

## CS0217

**binding lost in refactor** · error

A binding's declaration is gone and no candidate replaces it (the closest candidate, if any, scores below `heal.threshold`). During a refactor this keeps the refactor open. Restore the code, add the rename to a rename map (`--map`), or change the spec; `catspec sync --apply --partial` applies the rest meanwhile.

## CS0220

**unresolvable** · warning

CatSpec can't decide the check from syntax alone, for example a base type that is a type alias, a parameter without a type annotation, or a class without its own constructor that inherits one. It is never reported as a failure of the contract; its severity is `enforcement.unresolvable` (`warn` or `error`). Write the type explicitly to make it checkable.

## CS0300

**drift** · warning

The shape of a bound declaration (kind, name, bases, attributes, modifiers and member signatures; bodies excluded) changed since it was recorded in the spec's lock file, and the spec's binding didn't change with it. Implemented specs report it with the severity of `enforcement.drift` (`off`, `warn`, `strict`), in-progress specs as info. Run `catspec accept <spec-id>` to record an intended change, update the spec, or change the code back.

## CS0301

**regression of a satisfied item** · error

A contract item that passed before (recorded in `satisfied` of the spec's lock file) fails now. This is an error even while the spec is in progress (the ratchet, ADR-006): work in progress may be incomplete, but what already worked must not break. The message keeps the original code and text. Fix the code, or change the spec item (a changed item leaves `satisfied` until it passes again).

## CS0400

**waived** · info

A rule violation covered by a waiver (`waivers` in the spec, with a reason and an optional `until` date). It doesn't fail the check. The message keeps the original code and text.

## CS0401

**waiver expired** · error

A waiver's `until` date has passed. The violations it covered are reported again. Fix them and remove the waiver, or extend `until` with a reason.

## CS0502

**dependencies not satisfied** · error

`catspec status` refuses the transition: `ready` needs every `depends_on` spec to exist, `in-progress` and `implemented` need them `implemented` with passing contracts. The message names each dependency and why. `--force` skips this gate.

## CS0601

**forbidden call** · error

A `forbid_call` rule matched a call in its scope (`within` a binding or member, the spec's files, or `paths`). `*` in the pattern matches any text. Remove the call or add a waiver with a reason.

## CS0602

**required call missing** · error

A `require_call` rule found no matching call in its scope. Add the call.

## CS0603

**forbidden import** · error

A file matching the rule's `from` imports a module that `forbid_import` forbids, or that `allow_import_only` doesn't allow. Relative imports are resolved to repository paths before they are matched. Remove the import or move the code.

## CS0604

**naming rule violated** · error

A declaration whose kind and name match a `naming` rule doesn't satisfy its `implements`, `extends`, `attributes` or `in_path` requirement.

## CS0605

**symbol must not exist** · error

A `must_not_exist` rule found a declaration it forbids (usually a deprecated API). Remove it or rename it.

## CS0610

**query match** · error

A `query` rule with `expect: absent` matched, or one with `expect: present` found nothing, in its scope.

## CS0620

**test missing** · error

A `test` rule names a test symbol that doesn't exist in the code. Write the test or fix the symbol.

## CS0621

**test failed** · error

With `--run-tests`, the `tests.command` of `catspec.yaml` failed for a `test` rule. The command runs without a shell; `{test}` in it is replaced with the test symbol.

## CS0700

**invalid workflow config** · error

The `workflow:` section of `catspec.yaml` is invalid: an unknown preset, stage key, gate, status or placeholder (valid placeholders: `{feature}`, `{feature_dir}`, `{spec}`). The message names the value and suggests close matches. `catspec workflow doctor` also reports it as a warning when the preset doesn't match the repository (no `openspec/` folder for `openspec`, no `.specify/` for `spec-kit`).

## CS0701

**start gate failed** · error

`catspec stage start` (or MCP `start_stage`) refused the stage: one of its start gates failed. The message names the gate and why, followed by the diagnostics of the underlying check. Fix them and start the stage again; `--force` starts it anyway and logs the override.

## CS0702

**finish gate failed** · error

`catspec stage finish` (or MCP `finish_stage`) refused the stage: one of its finish gates failed, e.g. `contracts_pass` while a contract fails or `tasks_done` while a task is unticked. The status isn't changed. Fix what it reports and finish the stage again.

## CS0703

**implemented spec fails its final gates** · warning

An `implemented` spec in the commit no longer passes the built-in gates of its workflow's final stage (the one that sets `implemented`), e.g. a task was unticked. Reported by the pre-commit hook with the severity of `workflow.enforce_in_hook`; `command:` gates never run in the hook.

## CS0704

**driver not found** · error

`catspec workflow doctor` couldn't find what a stage needs: a skill's file (`<skills_dir>/<name>/SKILL.md`) or a command's program on PATH. The message names the skill or command and the expected path.

## CS0705

**stage out of order** · error

A stage was started or finished before an earlier stage is done (its finish gates pass and its status is reached). Run `catspec next <feature>` to see the current stage. `--force` overrides the order and logs the override.

## CS0706

**command gate skipped** · warning

A `command:` gate wasn't run because `workflow.allow_commands` is false (the default), so it doesn't block the stage. Run the command yourself, or set `workflow.allow_commands: true` to let CatSpec run it (without a shell).

## CS0901

**parse error in file** · warning

A source file has a syntax error at the reported location. CatSpec still uses the declarations it could read before and after the error, so results for that file may be incomplete. Fix the syntax error. A file larger than 1 MiB, or one the language adapter fails on, isn't parsed at all: it gets one CS0901 at its first line and no facts.

## CS0902

**git unavailable** · error

The command reads the git index or history (`catspec check --staged`, the pre-commit hook, `install-hooks`), but git can't be run: it isn't installed or isn't on PATH. Install git or fix PATH. CatSpec runs git without a shell.
